page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz under KVM hypervisor virtualization. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Cache memory allocation consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 32.0 GB, yielding a compute-dense memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance provides 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains zero local storage, and includes no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmark metrics show a distinction between single-threaded and parallel execution models. Single-core performance falls in the bottom 25% percentile, as observed in stress-ng single-core tests (1311.19) and single-threaded data compression tasks such as Gzip (22.76 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (8.81 GB/sec). Conversely, multi-core operations perform within the middle 50% average range, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 13975.48, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 7299.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 15380.43. Large block uncached memory operations deliver 88.67 GB/sec for reads and 45.93 GB/sec for writes.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance family a cost-efficient choice for parallelized processing tasks that do not demand extensive memory capacity per thread. While single-threaded computational throughput presents a bottleneck for sequential workloads, the 16 dedicated vCPUs deliver balanced multi-core density. Database and web serving benchmarks demonstrate stable throughput, including 13.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.29 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is well aligned for web server clusters, key-value caching layers, containerized microservices, and multi-threaded software compilation.
